page: Microsoft Azure D96als_v7 is a compute-focused general purpose virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is built on dedicated x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processors clocked up to 4.5 GHz, providing 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with dual multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, backed by vector and cryptographic extensions including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and AES.

System memory consists of 192.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio that aligns with compute-heavy architectures rather than memory-dense configurations. In synthetic stress-ng benchmarks, the instance achieves top-tier results in both single-core (3523.78) and multi-core (168119.86) execution. Memory throughput is marked by high cached bandwidth reaching 9132.42 GB/sec on small blocks and uncached write bandwidth of 172.54 GB/sec, while uncached large-block read operations deliver 307.93 GB/sec.

The D96als_v7 does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware accelerators, leaving 0.0 GPUs and requiring external network-attached storage volumes for file systems. Operational benchmarks confirm high instruction density, evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 109958.38 and Redis SET throughput exceeding 130 million operations per second. Static web serving reaches 90.41 GB/sec, while CPU-based inference executes 5203.52 tokens per second on prompt processing with a 135M parameter model.

With its low memory-to-vCPU ratio and zero local storage overhead, the D96als_v7 provides strong CPU performance density per resource allocation. The instance represents an efficient tradeoff for compute-bound scenarios that do not demand extensive RAM footprints or local NVMe scratch space. It is technically suited for CPU-bound compiling, media transcoding, static content distribution, high-throughput web serving, and distributed batch computing architectures.
description: Microsoft Azure D96als_v7 is a high-density compute-oriented instance powered by AMD EPYC 9V45 processors operating up to 4.5 GHz. Configured with 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores, the system allocates 192.0 GB of system RAM, resulting in a 2.0 GB per vCPU distribution. The virtual machine omits local storage and GPUs, relying on external disk attachments. Benchmark evaluations show top-decile CPU execution in stress-ng multi-core testing alongside strong uncached memory bandwidth. Data throughput reaches 130.74 million Redis operations per second and 90.41 GB/sec in static web delivery. Without the resource overhead of excess memory or local solid-state drives, D96als_v7 balances high parallel compute performance with resource-conscious deployment economics. This profile makes it directly suited for compute-intensive batch processing, software compilation, static web infrastructure, and algorithmic workloads.
